episodes.205131: A four corners high pressure advected a high amount of atmospheric moisture into the region. This was day one of an extended push of monsoon moisture that produced heavy rain, localized flooding, strong outflow winds.
episodes.205133: The second day of deep monsoonal moisture streaming north. Allowing for widespread flooding rains and locally strong thunderstorm winds.
episodes.205154: Higher monsoon moisture moved across northern New Mexico on August 24th. This resulted in a better coverage of shower and thunderstorm activity across the northern mountains. Slow moving thunderstorms in the Jemez Mountains resulted in some flash flooding and washed out roads near State Route 4 and 126.
episodes.205226: Thunderstorm activity over Elmore and Montgomery counties late on August 23 led to isolated flooding issues. Highway 14 west of Wetumpka had minor flooding after a couple inches of rain fell. Meanwhile, more extensive flooding took place around Meriwether Rd in Pike Road, with the roadway being closed after radar estimates of 4-5 of rain fell in the immediate area.
episodes.205276: A surface cold front and , cold upper low approached northern NY during the afternoon of August 24th. Scattered thunderstorms developed along the boundary with only one storm producing any severe reports of localized wind damage.
episodes.205395: Surface low pressure associated with a seasonably anomalous closed upper low dragged a cold front through the area, resulting in evening showers and thunderstorms. Most convection was sub-severe as MLCAPE and effective shear were marginal (300-600 J/g and 20kts), however, there was one severe storm east of Pittsburgh in Westmoreland county. Damaging winds were the only threat with convection.
episodes.205506: A severe thunderstorm track south across Lincoln County producing 1.75 inch hail. A second round of thunderstorms produced a 63 mph wind gust at the Limon airport.
episodes.205512: Strong monsoon thunderstorms caused wind damage in Yavapai County and some flash flooding in northern Coconino County.
episodes.205737: Thunderstorms moving through southern Lake Huron produced wind gusts to 35 knots.
episodes.205973: A lingering front across northeast Florida combined with daytime heating triggered strong storms in the afternoon that produced gusty downdraft winds.
episodes.206145: A broad belt of northwesterly flow aloft extended across the WFO Norman Forecast Area on the 24th. An embedded mid-level impulse instigated a round of intense severe weather across northwestern Oklahoma during the evening hours. This included a transient supercell thunderstorm that impacted portions of Woodward, Dewey and Custer Counties. This thunderstorm produced widespread wind damage, including observations of severe wind gusts exceeding 90 mph.
episodes.206405: A slow-moving cold front triggered the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across the area. An unstable environment with sufficient wind shear allows some storms to turn severe, producing damaging wind gusts and hail. One of the severe storms moved over the fairgrounds during the Great New York Fair leading to scattered damage on the grounds and one injury. Storms also led to the formation of a waterspout off of Lewis Point on Oneida Lake.
episodes.206597: The subtropical high pressure was situated near the Four Corners Region with south to southeasterly flow in place across much of southern CA. This southerly flow pulled in abundant moisture with Precipitable Water Values exceeding 1.5. The combination of the moisture and daytime heating resulted in MLCAPE in excess of 1000 J/KG with DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG. Widespread thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon across the San Diego Mountains and the northern Baja chain with an isolated severe thunderstorm erupting over southern portions of the Imperial Valley just southwest of El Centro. This thunderstorm was nearly stationary producing damaging winds and blowing dust.
episodes.206864: A stalled frontal boundary to the north of the region allowed for low pressure to influence weather over the area.
episodes.206874: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust in St Lucie County.
episodes.206878: Late morning into early afternoon thunderstorms within westerly sea breeze flow south of a stalled boundary along the northern Gulf Coast produce gusty marine winds over the Tampa Bay waters.
episodes.206918: Deep moisture residing across the area in advance of low pressure developing and passing off the coast led to an environment capable of flooding in poorly drained areas.
episodes.206967: A plume of anomalously rich monsoonal moisture pushed into eastern Utah and western Colorado in the days prior to these debris flows. On the day of the flows, precipitable water values were in excess of 1.00 inch across the region. Daytime heating acting on the complex terrain of the region allowed for the formation of thunderstorms during the afternoon. These storms were capable of producing heavy rainfall with very high rain rates. Over the course of the day, multiple of these storms moved over the recent Lee and Elk RBX burn scars in Rio Blanco county, triggering multiple debris flows.
episodes.207034: A severe thunderstorm formed and moved westward into Lukeville, AZ. The severe thunderstorm wind caused damage to equipment that caused the loss of power to 56 customers for an unknown duration of time.
episodes.207102: A lone severe thunderstorm dropped southward along the I-25 corridor in southern El Paso County producing strong winds and large hail.
episodes.207114: A slow moving stationary/cold front tracking east into the western New York area on the morning of August 24th, caused thunderstorms to develop over the eastern end of Lake Erie. Thunderstorms caused two waterspouts north to northeast of Barcelona Harbor.
episodes.207117: A slow moving cold front tracking east across the western and north central New York area on August 24th, caused strong to severe thunderstorms to develop. Severe thunderstorms resulted in wind damage and large hail for portions of the area east of the Genesee Valley.  Thunderstorms initially developed over the eastern end of Lake Erie during the morning hours and strengthened and expanded in coverage through the morning and into the afternoon as the cold front and thunderstorms pushed east. Increasing instability and shear ahead of the front, along with the forcing from the front caused the thunderstorms to reach severe limits.
episodes.207144: Storms developed along a 925-850 mb frontogenesis band and a surface moisture convergence zone. These storms congealed and moved southeastwardly across the CWA. When organized, severe wind gusts were generated in Hodgeman county.
episodes.207202: After an afternoon with a convective cloud line over the Lower Florida Keys, a slowly moving outflow boundary moved south, initiating substantial thunderstorm development just north of the Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.207203: Thunderstorms rapidly developed during the morning hours near Key Largo, producing isolated gale-force wind gusts and a waterspout.  The thunderstorms quickly collapsed.
episodes.207289: Southeasterly flow advected in monsoon moisture, fueling scattered thunderstorms, some of which produced severe winds and dust storm conditions.
episodes.207290: Southeasterly flow advected in monsoon moisture, fueling scattered thunderstorms. A few produced severe winds and dust storm conditions.
episodes.207336: Early afternoon thunderstorms within westerly sea breeze flow south of a stalled boundary along the northern Gulf Coast produce gusty winds resulting in wind damage at a mobile home park near Palmetto in Manatee County.
episodes.208195: An unseasonably cold air mass in the region for late August resulted in development of a couple waterspouts over the Great Lakes on the 24th.
